propositions: compact.py (798 LOC) bundles three unrelated responsibilities (compaction transaction, snapshot reconstruction, CLI surface) with cyclomatic complexity peaks of 24 and 21, creating a god command that blocks bugfixes and violates separation of concerns

split compact.py into compact_txn.py (transaction + shared snapshot primitives: _compact_locked, _build_authorship_ledger, _snapshot_strip_keys, _git_author, _git, _sync_before_compact) and compact_rebuild.py (reconstruction: rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log, _read_event_uuid, _REBUILD_COUNT) to enable acyclic dependencies and reduce complexity

counter re-export hazard: _REBUILD_COUNT and get_rebuild_count must co-locate in compact_rebuild.py (not compact.py) because rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log does global _REBUILD_COUNT; leaving the getter in facade creates silent failure (reads zero from different module global)

test monkeypatch hazard in test_compact_negative.py: setattr(_compact, '_git') and setattr(_compact.lock) must be repointed to compact_txn._git and _lock respectively after split, or patches silently fail to apply and tests pass while exercising nothing

public consumer paths (fsck_repair.py, fsck_restore.py, monkeypatch strings in test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py) must reach moved symbols through rebar._commands.compact re-exports to avoid editing external code

complexity-baseline.json entries for _compact_locked and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log must shrink or drop (shrink-only ratchet); new test must prove counter co-location by asserting get_rebuild_count increments across real rebuild call
